MARKET.head: Grape growers idle vineyards to cut costs as market demand weakens
MARKET.summ: Rather than abandoning vineyards amidst declining demand, some grape growers are pressing pause with the hopes of resuming production in a few years
takeaways: A 2025 study of 19 northern Willamette Valley vineyards found idling reduced management costs by an average of 38 percent per acre, with some sites cutting costs in half.
Vineyard idling, or mothballing production for one to three years, allows growers to preserve capital and avoid removal of vines when grape sales weaken but future demand is uncertain.

Successful idling requires careful vineyard maintenance: adequate year-round irrigation, aggressive pruning, weed control, and disease monitoring to ensure vines can resume production within two years.

MARKET.head: Early harvests reshape wine regions beyond the cellar and vineyard
MARKET.summ: Along with high temperatures, wine regions around the world reported new records for early grape harvests this summer. For some, it was weeks ahead of the traditional fall schedule, for others it was months in advance. In the heart of the Roussillon in France, Domaine Lafage started picking grapes on July 23, something...
takeaways: Harvests are arriving weeks or months early worldwide: Domaine Lafage in Roussillon picked on July 23 for the first time; Central Coast California harvested six to eight weeks early, the earliest in 27 years for grower Kevin Merrill.

Early harvest is raising costs across supply chains: electricity for cooling during peak summer heat, insurance, water fees, label application failures, and strain on bottling facilities and glass suppliers during high-temperature production periods.

MARKET.head: Federal THC limit threatens US hemp beverage retailers and manufacturers
MARKET.summ: Until recently, there was no federal guidance on the sale and consumption of hemp-derived THC-infused beverages, leading to a confusing, state-by-state patchwork of regulations
takeaways: Massachusetts retailer Art Nergaryan saw sales jump 25-35 percent after stocking THC beverages, then plummeted after state regulators banned cannabis drinks from wine and liquor stores in May 2024.
Congress enacted a federal limit of 0.4 milligrams THC per beverage container, effective November 12 2026, that will effectively ban most hemp-derived THC drinks currently on the market.
THC-infused beverage retail sales grew 135 percent in the 52 weeks prior to April 2026, reaching $239 million, but the category remains illegal under federal law despite state-by-state legalization.

MARKET.head: US tariff lift and India trade deal reshape Scotch market in 2026
MARKET.summ: Is it possible that 2026 could eventually be looked back on as the make-or-break year for Scotch whisky? In July, the U.S. finally lifted its 15 month tariff on Scotch, one that had contributed to a 15 percent decline in exports to this country, one of Scotland’s biggest international markets.
takeaways: US lifted 15-month tariff on Scotch in July 2026, reversing a 15 percent export decline to one of Scotland's largest markets.
July 2026 UK-India free trade agreement opened access to the world's largest whisky market with more affordable Scotch offerings.
Post-pandemic oversaturation and distillery closures like Clynelish persist despite tariff relief, though premiumization fatigue shifts focus to sub-$100 age-stated releases.

MARKET.head: Trump bans Canadian alcohol imports effective September 29
MARKET.summ: On Tuesday, president Donald Trump announced a plan to ban import of a range of Canadian products, escalating the already tense tariff disputes between the U.S. and its neighbor to the north. The restrictions , which are set to go into effect on Sept.
takeaways: President Donald Trump announced a ban on Canadian alcoholic beverages, dairy, and motor parts taking effect September 29, escalating ongoing tariff disputes.
The ban follows Canada's retaliatory 50 percent tariffs on US goods that began Tuesday, and prior failed trade negotiations in August.
A Canadian province-wide alcohol ban implemented in April 2024 already reduced US wine, beer, and spirits export revenue in 2025.

MARKET.head: American single malt ratification fails to lift sales as category battles broader whiskey slump
MARKET.summ: It’s been nearly two years since the Alcohol and Tobacco Tax and Trade Bureau (TTB) ratified a standard of identity for American single malt. The milestone was hailed as a victory by distillers across the country, many of whom had been petitioning the TTB for years via the American Single Malt Whiskey Commission (ASMWC).
takeaways: Ratification has helped with retail shelf placement and export tracking, yet consumer awareness outside connoisseur circles remains low and bourbon dominates American whiskey sales.

Distillers including Virginia Distillery Company and Whiskey Del Bac are diversifying into lower-priced cask-finished malts, blended spirits, and other categories as American single malt growth stalls.

CULTURE.head: Campania's white wines gain ground as lighter, mineral-driven styles gain favour
CULTURE.summ: Campania, the southern Italian region on the Tyrrhenian Sea, is perhaps best known for Aglianico, the marvelous red variety that is sometimes referred to as “the Barolo of the South.” If you haven’t tried Aglianico, here are some recommendations from my column earlier this year. Beyond Aglianico, Campania, with its volcanic...
takeaways: Campania's white varieties, Fiano, Greco, Falanghina, Coda di Volpe, are unoaked, stainless-steel aged, and marked by high acidity and minerality from volcanic soils near Mount Vesuvius and Mount Taburno.
The region's hilly terrain and volcanic terroir produce crisp, fresh wines comparable in style to Etna Biancos from Sicily, with prices often under €20.
Wine lovers increasingly gravitating toward lighter, lower-alcohol whites are discovering Campania's offerings as an obvious choice for everyday drinking and food pairing.

CULTURE.head: VinePair names 30 best Sauvignon Blancs, signals shift toward texture and depth
CULTURE.summ: Sauvignon Blanc has been here in the U.S. for a long time. From when viticulturist Charles Wetmore, founder of Cresta Blanca Winery, imported original grape cuttings from Bordeaux’s famed Château d’Yquem in the 19th century to when Robert Mondavi coined the rich, oak-aged Fumé Blanc style in Napa Valley.
takeaways: VinePair's annual tasting panel scored hundreds of Sauvignon Blancs on a 100-point scale, then compiled an editorially driven list of 30 best bottles by quality, price, and availability.
Virginia emerged as a standout region in 2026, with producers like Dogwood & Thistle and Emily Hodson crafting expressive, balanced wines that punch above their price point.

Loire Valley, Friuli, Napa, Oregon, Santa Barbara, Colorado, and Slovenia all represented, signaling a global shift toward Sauvignon Blancs with more texture and depth than the flinty, angular styles of the past.

CULTURE.head: AriZona Iced Tea launches artist residency at Woodbury headquarters
CULTURE.summ: Any marketing executive will tell you that they care about their brand’s aesthetics, but it’s rare to find a corporation where the design language is as distinctive, long-lasting, and personal as AriZona Iced Tea , a commitment that has recently taken an unexpected turn. AriZona Iced Tea entered the market in 1992 with cans...
takeaways: AriZona launched a six-week artist residency program at its Woodbury, N.Y. headquarters, hosting up to four artists per session with stipends, housing, studio access, and materials.

Three cohorts have completed the program since July 2025, with participants including Eleanor Dexter and Lucas Carlo Monasterio creating paintings, silkscreen work, and mixed-media pieces inspired by the brand's Southwest aesthetic.

Artists' work enters AriZona's permanent collection and is exhibited on-site; the residency extends the founders' legacy of personal, in-house design decisions as a competitive strategy separate from typical corporate marketing.

SCIENCE.head: Seven volcanic wine regions rival Mount Etna for mineral complexity
SCIENCE.summ: Mount Etna’s recent eruption reminded the world just how powerful volcanoes can be. For wine lovers, lava flow isn’t something to fear; rather, it’s celebrated as the source of compelling terroir. And while Etna, even when not exploding, often steals the spotlight, other regions around the world boast these unique soils.
takeaways: Volcanic soils from ancient and active eruptions create complex, layered terroirs that produce high-acidity wines with savory, mineral, and saline flavors distinct from other regions.
Santorini, Soave, the Canary Islands, Tokaji, Willamette Valley, Auvergne, and Lake County all show how volcanic geology shapes grape varieties, vine training methods, and final wine character.

Volcanic terrain's natural pest and disease resistance enables organic farming and preservation of old indigenous varieties, while challenging topography requires specialized viticulture techniques like basket training and hand-dug vine holes.

SCIENCE.head: Pierce's disease detected in European vineyards as climate risk zone expands
SCIENCE.summ: As warming temperatures increase the risk of Pierce’s disease in European vineyards, researchers and growers are looking to California for lessons in detection, prevention, and management
takeaways: Xylella fastidiosa bacterium, which causes Pierce's disease in grapevines, was detected in continental Europe in 2023 when a single infected vine appeared in Portugal; cases now persist in Spain, Italy, Portugal, and France.

Climate modeling suggests 41.2 percent of European vineyards face Pierce's disease risk, up from 21.8 percent in earlier estimates, with riverside and valley microclimates especially vulnerable as warming winters allow the pathogen to survive.

NEWSLETTERS.head: A big tasting of Tenerife wines, with some nice surprises
NEWSLETTERS.summ: As part of the recent Island Wines Summit in Tenerife we had a chance to taste through a range of
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jamie Goode
takeaways: Tenerife's highest vineyard at 1650 m produces Piedra Fluida Los Frontones, a stony, mineral wine with high acidity and distinctive character.
Many Tenerife wines feature ungrafted vines and saline, mineral characteristics; key producers include Artifice, Envinate, and Bodega El Lomo.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Raising Standards
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Joy is unconfined, one assumes, in the Languedoc village of Montpeyroux: last week it became the 369th French Appellation d’Origine Controlée. This will mean stricter controls on the red grapes used - but you can go wild and use 10% Counoise! - and maximum yields of 45 hectolitres per hectare.
NEWSLETTERS.author: Tim Atkin MW
takeaways: Montpeyroux became France's 369th AOC appellation, imposing stricter red grape controls and 45 hectolitre-per-hectare maximum yields on the Languedoc commune.

Muscadet rebuilt its reputation through producer-led creation of ten site-specific crus from 2011, better techniques, and natural attrition reducing producers from 700 to fewer than 300 since the early 1990s.
Soave created 33 geographical crus (UGAs) in 2020 and a DOCG tier in 2001, but producers remain confused about designations and consumer perception remains uncertain.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Of Substack & wine
NEWSLETTERS.summ: All that’s being poured for your reading enjoyment in what is currently the most dynamic platform for wine media
NEWSLETTERS.author: Miquel Hudin
takeaways: Substack created a Wine & Spirits subsection within its Rising and Top lists, separating wine content from the broader Food & Drink category to improve discovery.
Natural wine publications are among the top earners on Substack, though recent entrants to the category don't match established publishers' numbers.
Matthew Jukes, a traditional wine media figure, passed away last month.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Remembering Branko Čotar
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Slovenia lost a seminal winemaker from the Karst. I share my memories and his story
NEWSLETTERS.author: Simon J. Woolf
takeaways: Branko Čotar, pioneering natural winemaker from Slovenia's Karst region, died aged 78 on 27 August following a short illness.
Čotar began with 500 vines for his restaurant in 1974, started bottling in 1990, and built the winery to produce around 30,000 bottles annually.
He skin-fermented white grapes organically with no added sulphites decades before Radikon and Gravner popularized the practice in the late 1990s.

NEWSLETTERS.head: M is for Method
NEWSLETTERS.summ: The winemaking method speaks volumes about what you’ll find in the glass
NEWSLETTERS.author: Meg Maker
takeaways: Traditional method sparkling wines undergo second fermentation in bottle with sugar and yeast, then are disgorged and dosed; they develop nutty, complex flavors from bottle conditioning and aging.
Tank method (Charmat/Martinotti) uses pressurized tanks for second fermentation, producing cleaner, fresher sparkling wines with less lees contact than traditional method.
Skin-contact wines macerate white grapes with skins and seeds during fermentation, creating color and tannin; the tradition originated in the Caucasus and has resurged in the past two decades.
